title: {chip:alien-higgs-9:name} UHF Inlay — 688-bit User Memory
summary: The Alien long-range UHF chip UHF inlays embed Alien Technology's {chip:alien-higgs-9:short_name} chip with 128-bit EPC, 96-bit factory-serialised TID, and 688-bit (≥64 byte) user memory — the largest user memory in the volume RAIN RFID chip tier. They are the chip choice when on-tag data storage matters more than read-range floor: returnable transit item (RTI) tracking with trip-specific data, industrial asset records that work offline, field-service maintenance logs in mines / oil rigs / utility plants where network connectivity is unreliable, and multi-party GS1 Application Identifier data exchange. It serves as the chip / user-memory / on-tag-data-pattern / Higgs-9-vs-M700-vs-UCODE-9 selection reference for supply-chain, logistics, industrial asset, and offline-RFID deployments.

brief.label: Chip silicon and lineage
items: Alien Technology {chip:alien-higgs-9:short_name} — fourth-generation Alien RAIN RFID silicon, successor to {chip:alien-higgs-3:short_name} / Higgs-4 / {chip:alien-higgs-ec:short_name} family.
Manufactured at production volume since 2018; widely deployed across logistics, industrial, RTI, and field-service applications.
EPCglobal Gen2v2 / ISO/IEC 18000-63:2015 air-interface compliant; backward-compatible with all standards-compliant readers.

brief.label: Memory architecture
items: 128-bit EPC — supports SGTIN-96 / SGTIN-198 / SSCC-96 / GIAI-96 encoding per GS1 Tag Data Standard 2.0.
96-bit factory-serialised TID — globally unique immutable identifier for inventory deduplication and anti-cloning audit trail.
688-bit (≥64 byte) user memory — largest in volume RAIN RFID category; expandable on some variants to 256 bytes / 2048-bit.
32-bit access password + 32-bit kill password per EPC Gen2v2.

brief.label: Sensitivity and read range
items: Read sensitivity {chip:alien-higgs-9:read_sensitivity_dbm} dBm typical ({chip:alien-higgs-9:name} datasheet) — ~0.5 dB more sensitive than {chip:impinj-m770:name} (-22.7 dBm).
Free-air bench: 10-15 m read range with standard 6 dBic antenna at 4 W EIRP.
Real-world: 8-12 m logistics dock door, 5-9 m warehouse portal, 4-7 m retail apparel, 2-4 m on-metal / on-liquid with appropriate antenna.
Dense-reader mode (DRM) support ensures reliable operation in environments with multiple overlapping reader zones.

brief.label: Air interface and standards
items: ISO/IEC 18000-63:2015 + EPC Gen2v2 air interface (basic feature set; AUTHENTICATE not implemented).
GS1 EPC Tag Data Standard (TDS) 2.0 SGTIN-96 / SGTIN-198 / SSCC / GIAI / Application Identifier encoding.
EPCIS 2.0 supply-chain event data standard for RTI / pharma traceability integration.
Frequency: 860-960 MHz across FCC + ETSI + Japan + China sub-bands.

brief.label: On-tag data storage patterns — when user memory earns its premium
items: RTI trip data on pallets and roll cages: origin, destination, consignee, weight, gross/tare, trip number, timestamp — typically 32-48 bytes fits comfortably in {chip:alien-higgs-9:short_name} user memory.

Field-service and utility asset records: last service date, next service date, serial, calibration status, technician ID — written by handheld readers in the field, works offline in tunnels / mines / remote utility plants.

Closed-loop pharma and medical-device traceability: lot code, manufacture date, expiry date, sterilisation cycle counter — on-tag writable fields enable compliance audits even when cloud serialisation is unreachable.
GS1 Application Identifiers for multi-party data exchange: AI (01) GTIN, AI (10) lot, AI (17) expiry, AI (21) serial written directly to user memory in AFI format per GS1 EPC TDS.

Anti-patterns to avoid: don't write customer PII (no auth floor — anyone with reader reads it); don't use user memory as primary identifier (use TID); don't rely on user memory for authentication (no crypto on Gen2 basic chips).

brief.label: {chip:alien-higgs-9:short_name} vs Impinj M700 vs {chip:nxp-ucode-9:short_name} — when each one wins
items: {chip:alien-higgs-9:short_name}: when user memory is the deciding factor. 688-bit (vs M700's 32-bit, {chip:nxp-ucode-9:short_name}'s 32-224-bit configurable) is the largest in the volume RAIN tier — default for RTI / industrial asset / offline-write applications.

Impinj M700 ({chip:impinj-m730:short_name} / {chip:impinj-m750:short_name} / {chip:impinj-m770:short_name}): when small-antenna read range is the deciding factor. -22.1 to -22.7 dBm sensitivity is competitive on miniaturised antennas; jewellery / pharma vials / small-item retail.

{chip:nxp-ucode-9:name}: when unit-cost at very high volume is the deciding factor. Typically 10-15% below {chip:alien-higgs-9:short_name} per chip at >100M units; volume choice for pure EPC-only retail apparel without user memory.
All three share ISO/IEC 18000-63:2015 Gen2v2 air interface — swap decisions driven by antenna design, user memory, sensitivity floor, per-unit pricing — not reader-fleet compatibility.

Cryptographic authentication is not a shipping feature on {chip:alien-higgs-9:short_name}, M700, M800 ({chip:impinj-m830:short_name} / {chip:impinj-m850:short_name}), or {chip:nxp-ucode-9:short_name} — programmes requiring per-tap cryptographic authentication today specify HF chips such as {chip:nxp-ntag-424-dna:name} or UCODE DNA, not UHF.

brief.label: Industrial asset tracking
items: Mines, oil rigs, construction sites, remote agriculture — environments lacking reliable network connectivity.
On-tag data storage allows handheld readers to write and read application data locally without server communication.
Maintenance scheduling, calibration tracking, safety-inspection logs all live on the chip; backend sync occurs when connectivity returns.

brief.label: Returnable transit items (RTI) and logistics
items: Pallets, containers, roll cages, IBCs — RTI tagging requires trip-specific data (origin, destination, contents, weight) that changes every cycle.
{chip:alien-higgs-9:short_name}'s large user memory accommodates this dynamic data without cloud dependency.
Multi-tenant logistics environments where tags transit between organisations need standardised data fields each party can read and write — GS1 AI format on user memory.

brief.label: Antenna designs available
items: 12+ standard antenna configurations: general-purpose far-field (20 × 20 to 100 × 20 mm), compact retail, on-metal industrial, flexible / wearable, ultra-long-range logistics.
Custom antenna engineering 4-8 weeks for specialised applications.
ARC Master List spec category certified across multiple antenna designs.

brief.label: Form factors — dry, wet, converted-label
items: Dry inlay: bare antenna + chip on carrier substrate, no adhesive — for label converters laminating into their own construction.
Wet inlay: pressure-sensitive adhesive on release liner, ready to apply directly.
Converted label: printed face stock + adhesive + inlay = finished branded label.
Hard-tag housings: weatherproof / impact-resistant industrial housings for RTI / asset programmes.

brief.label: Procurement and lead times
items: Prototype quantities 100+ pieces; production volume 50M+ units annually.
Lead time 20-30 business days for standard antenna on 5-10M unit orders; 45-60 days during chip-supply constraint or volumes >20M.
Blanket PO with call-off quantities recommended for programmes >10M / year — locks allocation, enables pitch / antenna fine-tuning.

brief.label: Compliance posture
items: EPC Gen2v2 (ISO/IEC 18000-63:2015) air-interface compliance.
GS1 TDS 2.0 SGTIN / SSCC / GIAI / Application Identifier encoding.
Reader-side regulatory: FCC 47 CFR Part 15.247 (US 902-928 MHz), ETSI EN 302 208 (EU 865-868 MHz), ARIB STD-T106 (Japan).
Auburn University RFID Lab ARC Master List certification for retail-grade performance benchmarks where applicable.

Extended power management with {chip:alien-higgs-9:read_sensitivity_dbm} dBm read sensitivity (~0.5 dB more sensitive than M700-series) delivers 10-15 m read range with standard 6 dBic antennas at 4 W EIRP. items.label: User memory (largest in volume RAIN tier)

bullets: Logistics + supply chain operations with large dock doors, high ceilings, fast-moving conveyors need consistent reads at 8-15 m — {chip:alien-higgs-9:short_name} sensitivity + DRM maintain >99% read rates in dense-tag environments.
Industrial environments (mines, oil rigs, construction, remote agriculture) often lack reliable network connectivity; on-tag data storage lets handhelds work offline without server round-trip.

sections.title: When 688 bits actually earns its premium

dataHighlight.heading: Typical RTI trip data fitting comfortably in {chip:alien-higgs-9:short_name} user memory
dataHighlight.text: A returnable transit item (pallet, container, roll cage) typically carries trip-specific data: 4 bytes origin code + 4 bytes destination + 8 bytes consignee + 4 bytes weight + 4 bytes gross / tare + 4 bytes trip number + 8 bytes timestamp = 36 bytes. That fits comfortably in {chip:alien-higgs-9:short_name}'s 64-byte (688-bit) user memory with room for additional fields like temperature-log summary, sterilisation cycle counter, last-cleaning-cycle timestamp, or AI-encoded multi-party fields. The same 36 bytes does NOT fit in M700's 32-bit (4-byte) user memory or {chip:nxp-ucode-9:short_name}'s small-config user memory, forcing those programmes to either truncate data, run a backend round-trip per scan, or use a different chip. {chip:alien-higgs-9:short_name}'s structural value is that the entire trip context lives on the tag, readable by any party with a standards-compliant reader, modifiable by authorised parties holding the access password — without backend dependency. For applications without that requirement (pure-EPC retail, simple inventory scan), M700 or {chip:nxp-ucode-9:short_name} wins on cost. The chip-family decision pivots on whether the application reads on-tag data offline.
dataHighlight.source: GS1 EPC TDS 2.0 + EPCIS 2.0 + {chip:alien-higgs-9:name} product brief + Proud Tek RTI deployment references

bullets: RTI trip data: origin / destination / consignee / weight / trip number / timestamp = 32-48 bytes typical.
Field-service logs: service date / next-service / serial / calibration / technician = 30-40 bytes.
Pharma traceability: lot / mfg date / expiry / sterilisation counter = 20-30 bytes.
GS1 AI multi-party: AI(01) + AI(10) + AI(17) + AI(21) = 30-40 bytes.
All fit comfortably in 64-byte {chip:alien-higgs-9:short_name} user memory — none fit in M700's 32-bit user.

sections.title: From {chip:alien-higgs-3:short_name} 2007 to {chip:alien-higgs-9:short_name} as RTI / industrial-asset default

items.text: EPC Gen2 v1 standardised through EPCglobal; ISO/IEC 18000-63 Type C ratified subsequently. Alien Technology emerges as one of three dominant RAIN RFID silicon vendors alongside Impinj and NXP.

{chip:alien-higgs-3:name} (ALN-9640) launches with 512-bit user memory (800-bit total NVM across EPC + user + TID + reserve banks per {chip:alien-higgs-3:short_name} datasheet) establishing Alien's positioning as the large-user-memory choice in the UHF chip ecosystem.

Walmart Phase 1 RFID pilot drives apparel item-level adoption; supply-chain RTI programmes scale on {chip:alien-higgs-3:short_name} / Higgs-4 silicon — large user memory establishes operational pattern for RTI trip-data storage.
ISO/IEC 18000-63:2015 publishes; Higgs family migrates forward through {chip:alien-higgs-ec:short_name} and Higgs-4 generations maintaining the large-user-memory positioning.

{chip:alien-higgs-9:name} launches with 688-bit user memory + {chip:alien-higgs-9:read_sensitivity_dbm} dBm read sensitivity + DRM — the current-generation chip behind RTI / industrial / field-service deployments.

Walmart RFID source-tag mandate scales across categories; {chip:alien-higgs-9:short_name} captures the user-memory-dependent supply-chain segment while Impinj M700 / {chip:nxp-ucode-9:name} dominate pure-EPC retail. Auburn ARC Master List certifications validate {chip:alien-higgs-9:short_name} across multiple antenna designs.

items.label: 2026 Today
items.text: Cross-buyer reference experience on aerospace-part-traceability, DPP-textile-EU-ESPR, automotive-component-RFID, healthcare-instrument, and multi-application-on-tag programmes shows converge on {chip:alien-higgs-9:short_name} silicon + ARC-certified antenna + on-tag user-memory data pattern (GS1 AI / RTI trip data / field-service log) + EPC Gen2v2 reader fleet as the operator-side template. M700 / {chip:nxp-ucode-9:short_name} run as alternatives on user-memory-light retail; programmes requiring per-tap cryptographic authentication move off UHF entirely to HF ({chip:nxp-ntag-424-dna:short_name} / UCODE DNA).

sections.title: Inside the inlay — dipole, strap, and where the 688 bits live
sections.intro: A UHF RAIN inlay is unglamorous hardware: a copper dipole, a grain-of-sand die flip-chipped to a strap, and a substrate to hold them flat. Everything you pay a premium for hides in that speck of silicon — which is why the [full UHF chip comparison](/compare/ucode8-vs-ucode9-vs-monza-r6-vs-higgs9/) is really a memory-and-sensitivity argument, not an antenna one.

image.alt: Flat anatomy of a UHF RAIN inlay: a copper or aluminium dipole antenna tuned 860-960 MHz on a PET or paper substrate, a flip-chip strap carrying the Higgs-9 die at the centre, and the three delivery forms — dry inlay, wet inlay, converted label.

bullets: Dry inlay — bare antenna and chip on the carrier, no adhesive; the form label converters laminate into their own construction.
Wet inlay — pressure-sensitive adhesive on a release liner, ready to apply directly to the item.
Converted label — printed face stock over the inlay, delivered as a finished branded label.
12+ standard antenna designs from 20 × 20 mm compact to 100 × 20 mm long-range; the Higgs-9 die is constant, the antenna sets the read range.

sections.title: The four memory banks — EPC, TID, and that headline User bank
sections.intro: EPC Gen2v2 gives every RAIN tag the same four memory banks. On a cost-optimised chip the User bank is a rounding error; on Higgs-9 it is the reason the SKU exists — 688 bits, the largest in the volume RAIN tier, enough to carry a whole [returnable-transit-item](/industries/logistics/) trip record on the tag itself.

image.alt: The four EPC Gen2v2 memory banks of the Higgs-9 drawn to scale: Reserved 64-bit passwords, EPC 128-bit, TID 96-bit, and the dominant User bank at 688-bit, annotated that a 36-byte RTI trip record fits the User bank but not an M700 32-bit User bank.

rows: Largest in volume RAIN tier; RTI trip data, GS1 AI

bullets: RTI trip data — origin, destination, consignee, weight, trip number, timestamp — is 32-48 bytes and lives entirely on the tag.
Field-service logs (service date, serial, calibration, technician) run 30-40 bytes; pharma lot / expiry / sterilisation fields 20-30 bytes.
GS1 Application Identifiers — AI (01) GTIN, AI (10) lot, AI (17) expiry, AI (21) serial — write straight to User memory for multi-party exchange.
None of these fit an M700 32-bit User bank — offline on-tag data is where Higgs-9 stops being interchangeable.

faq.question: What is the difference between {chip:alien-higgs-9:name} and Impinj M700?
faq.answer: Both are high-performance RAIN RFID chips. {chip:alien-higgs-9:short_name} offers significantly larger user memory (688 bits / 64+ bytes vs M700's 0-32 bits) and slightly higher sensitivity (-23.2 dBm typical vs {chip:impinj-m770:short_name}'s -22.7 dBm) — better for applications needing on-tag data storage and longer raw read range. M700 ({chip:impinj-m730:short_name} / {chip:impinj-m750:short_name} / {chip:impinj-m770:short_name}) offers smaller silicon footprint advantages on miniaturised antennas — better for small-antenna applications (jewellery, pharma vials, small-item retail). Choose by whether on-tag user memory dominates the use case ({chip:alien-higgs-9:short_name}) or whether small-antenna read range matters more (M700).

faq.question: Can I store custom application data on the {chip:alien-higgs-9:short_name} chip?
faq.answer: Yes — {chip:alien-higgs-9:user_bits}-bit (≥64-byte) user memory bank is fully read/write accessible. Store custom data fields: asset ID, maintenance date, calibration status, trip origin/destination, weight, temperature log summary, sterilisation cycle counter, GS1 Application Identifier multi-party fields. Data persists without power and reads on any standards-compliant UHF RFID reader. Authentication: standard 32-bit access password required for write access on locked memory blocks; not cryptographically secure (anyone with reader and the access password can read/write) — see anti-pattern guidance in the brief section.

faq.question: What antenna designs are available for the {chip:alien-higgs-9:short_name}?
faq.answer: 12+ standard antenna designs: general-purpose far-field (20 × 20 mm to 100 × 20 mm), compact retail, on-metal industrial, flexible / wearable, windshield, ultra-long-range logistics. Custom antenna designs available with 4-8 week development timelines. ARC Master List spec category certifications across multiple antenna designs for retail-grade performance benchmarks.

faq.question: Does the {chip:alien-higgs-9:short_name} support per-tap cryptographic authentication?
faq.answer: No — {chip:alien-higgs-9:short_name} implements the ISO/IEC 18000-63 Gen2v2 base command set (including standard access / kill passwords) but does NOT implement cryptographic mutual authentication. This isn't a Higgs-9-specific gap: per-tap cryptographic authentication is not a shipping feature on any mainstream UHF RAIN RFID chip today ({chip:alien-higgs-9:short_name}, M700, M800 / {chip:impinj-m830:short_name} / {chip:impinj-m850:short_name}, {chip:nxp-ucode-9:short_name}). Programmes requiring it (pharmaceutical serialisation per DSCSA / EU FMD, luxury anti-counterfeit, high-value spare-parts authentication) specify HF chips such as {chip:nxp-ntag-424-dna:name} or UCODE DNA on a separate frequency band — typically alongside, not instead of, a UHF inventory tag. {chip:alien-higgs-9:short_name} remains appropriate for supply-chain, logistics, industrial asset tracking, and RTI applications where the threat model doesn't require per-tap cryptographic authentication.

faq.question: What is the lead time for a 5-10 million unit {chip:alien-higgs-9:short_name} order?
faq.answer: Production lead time typically 20-30 business days for standard antenna designs on 5-10M unit orders, allocated against Alien's chip-supply release schedule. Higher volumes (>20M) or chip-supply constraint periods: quote-to-ship can extend to 45-60 business days. Recommendation: blanket PO with call-off quantities rather than single spot buy for programmes >10M units / year — locks allocation, enables pitch / antenna fine-tuning during allocation window. For urgent needs, {chip:nxp-ucode-9:name} or {chip:impinj-m730:name} / M750 inlays on the same antenna design substitute with 2-4 week re-tune qualification.

faq.question: How do I encode GS1 Application Identifiers on {chip:alien-higgs-9:short_name} user memory?
faq.answer: Use the AFI (Application Family Identifier) format per GS1 EPC TDS 2.0. Common pattern: write AI (01) GTIN-14 in first user-memory block, AI (10) lot in second, AI (17) expiry in third, AI (21) serial in fourth. Each AI tagged with its 2-4 character identifier prefix per GS1 General Specifications. Multi-party supply-chain participants read standardised fields without custom integration; each party knows AI (01) is GTIN regardless of who wrote it. EPCIS 2.0 event submission completes the digital twin loop for participants with backend connectivity.
